strongest_angle: In 1963, 17-year-old Elizabeth Tyler captured striking photographs of Coventry's bomb sites using a second-hand camera bought with waitress wages, an archive that was later found in an attic after six decades.

key_facts.fact: In 1963, 17-year-old Elizabeth Tyler wandered the streets of Coventry capturing images of the city's bomb sites and abandoned buildings.
Elizabeth Tyler was homeless, an orphan, and studying at Coventry College of Art while using a second-hand camera bought from her first wages as a waitress.
The images from Coventry survived being moved to four different countries over six decades and remained untouched in a box in an attic.
Elizabeth Tyler developed her films in the Coventry College of Art darkroom each evening after photographing old bomb sites with a 1933 Rolleicord camera.
